Lemma
[radial geodesics minimize, polar form]

↗ lem:dc-ch3-3-6-radius ↗ lem:dc-ch3-3-6-rayspeed

1. ch3:3.6There is $\rho >0$ (a Gauss ball for $\exp _p$) such that for every $v$ with $\| v\| <\rho $ and every competing curve given in polar form through the exponential chart — a differentiable $w:[0,1]\to B_\rho (0)\subset T_pM$ with continuous derivative, $w(0)=0$, $w(1)=v$ — the chart-read length of the radial geodesic $\gamma (t)=\exp _p(tv)$ is at most that of $c(t)=\exp _p(w(t))$: \[ \ell (\gamma )=\int _0^1\sqrt{\langle \dot\gamma ,\dot\gamma \rangle }\, dt \; \le \; \int _0^1\sqrt{\langle \dot c,\dot c\rangle }\, dt=\ell (c). \]
Proof

\sketch

By subsection 2.1, $\ell (\gamma )=|v|_p$. By the radius comparison (subsection 2.1),

\[ \ell (c)\; \ge \; r(1)-r(0)=|w(1)|_p-|w(0)|_p=|v|_p-0=\ell (\gamma ). \]

□
